newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chips edge higher after strong economic report.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chips edge higher after strong economic report.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks edged higher Friday after investors largely shrugged off a surprisingly strong rise in orders for expensive durable goods in September.

The Dow Jones industrial average rose 11.93 points to 6,004.41 just after 1 p.m. The broader market was mixed, with declining issues outnumbering advances by an 11-10 margin on moderate volume of about 208 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
Stocks got a modest lift from bonds, which rallied despite the stronger-than-expected durable goods report.

The Commerce Department said orders for big-ticket items like cars and refrigerators jumped 4.6 percent in September -- more than double the 2 percent forecast by economists -- as strong demand for aircraft more than erased a weak showing in August.

The report initially sent the bond market skidding but cooler heads soon prevailed and bonds staged a quick recovery to move higher. Signs of unexpected economic strength worry bond investors concerned that inflation will erode returns on their investments.
"It's a stronger-than-expected figure, but when you look at the breakdown it's nothing remarkable ... mainly due to aircraft," said David Sloan, senior economist at I.D.E.A. Inc.

"It was a very big number but you have to remember two things -- it's a September number and it's a very, very volatile and unpredictable number," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp.

After falling earlier, the 30-year Treasury bond rose 14/32, or $4.375 on a $1,000 bond, lowering its yield, which moves in the opposite direction from the price, to 6.82 percent from 6.85 percent on Thursday.
With worries over the report fading, stocks spent the early afternoon locked in a tight range as investors braced for a slew of economic reports next week.
But analysts warned that the recent profit-taking that has pulled the Dow industrials down about 100 points this week week was probably not over yet.

"One thing to note is that technically the market is starting to exhibit some weakness," said Chris Dickerson at Global Market Strategists Inc. "Psychologically, if we close below 6,000 today it would be negative from a short term point of view."

With volume barely near 200 million shares at midday, the market was considerably quieter than in recent sessions, analysts noted, a sign that some investors were moving to the sidelines, at least for now.
The Nasdaq composite index fell 0.68 point to 1,226.32.
The American Stock Exchange index was off 0.86 point at 568.94.
